comment: Single source of truth for trigger cadence. Read by three consumers:
1. infra/trigger-worker/ decides which workflows are due and dispatches them.
3. tests/test_trigger_alignment.py asserts every entry here has a matching workflow file
that declares workflow_dispatch with a source input.
Two copies of a cadence is a bug waiting to happen, so there is one copy, here.
schedule_only_cadence_minutes is what GitHub's own scheduler actually delivers, not what
the cron expression asks for. Measured on attempt 1: 3.9 to 5.3 percent delivery for high
frequency crons, 4.68 hour median delay. See ARCHITECTURE.md section 1a. The page states
whichever cadence is actually armed, which is why both numbers live here.

workflows.name: heartbeat
workflows.note: Phase 0 proof, then the permanent freshness signal. Never gated: if this is off, the page cannot tell the difference between a stopped pipeline and a stopped heartbeat.

workflows.name: ingest-thermal
workflows.note: FIRMS NOAA-20 primary, NOAA-21 and MODIS for corroboration.

workflows.name: ingest-weekly
workflows.note: GLAD and RADD. Pin dataset versions explicitly, cadence is irregular.

workflows.name: ingest-atmospheric
workflows.note: OpenAQ, plus Sentinel-5P via Planetary Computer later.

workflows.name: ingest-marine
workflows.note: Global Fishing Watch. Cap request volume in code: a daily breach is a 24 hour block, a monthly breach is 30 days.

workflows.name: confirm
workflows.note: GDELT bulk GKG with a local relevance filter. Its own workflow so a slow index can never delay detection. Honours GKG_READ_LAG_MINUTES.
